title: Hand your honor back to the Master
summary: The servant does not have to manufacture dignity in every room. Nanak places honor and greatness in the Master’s hands, where pride can stop arguing for itself.
takeaway: Hand your honor back to the Master you serve.
lifeApplication: When pride starts rehearsing its defense, pause and say, “I am Your servant.” Let that belonging decide how much you need to prove.

source.shortMeaning: The servant’s honor and glory belong to the Lord and Master.
source.lifeApplication: When bruised pride flares, hand your honor back to the One you serve.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad grounds dignity in belonging to the Master rather than in the room’s recognition.
evidence.turn: Let service make honor received instead of defended.
evidence.practicalImplication: When pride starts rehearsing its defense, pause and say, “I am Your servant.” Let that belonging decide how much you need to prove.
